findings.finding: Read PDF pages 1, 3, 5 and 9: violin I opening and Lento/Presto ending, violin II middle, violin III ending. First violin has rapid articulated high-register passagework, octave-transposed ascent, repeated double stops and chords; violin II also has agile crossing figures and ornaments. Third violin supports the texture with double stops but has fewer upper-register demands.

grade.basis: Actual notation sampled across all three parts, including opening, contrasting slow music and final Presto. Diploma-level judgment rests on recurrent fast high-register bow articulation and double-stop intonation, rather than an isolated bar. Tempo transitions, exposed three-violin tuning and shared articulation need experienced ensemble playing; no extra level added. Four-page bounded sample, not a complete bar-by-bar technical audit.

findings.finding: Read four actual music pages: PDF pages 2, 3, 5 and 7 (opening, continuation, later reprise and ending). Allegro molto repeatedly uses upper-register running figures, chromatic turns, trills, double stops, octave-transposed passages and wide registral jumps; the ending sustains this agility rather than presenting only one exceptional bar. This file contains violin I only, so the relative difficulty of violins II and III is unverified.

grade.basis: First-violin notation supports a provisional diploma-level assessment through sustained Allegro molto facility, chromatic upper-register intonation, double-stop control and rapid register changes. No ensemble uplift applied. Sampled four music pages spanning the first part; other parts unavailable in the supplied score, so violin 1 as the whole-work hardest part is a hypothesis, and approval is held pending comparison with violins II and III. Level 7 is supported for the inspected first part, not a verified upper bound for the complete trio.
